sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: (a) When a system absorbs 50 kJ of heat and does 30 kJ of work, find ΔU. (b) If the bond enthalpies of C–H and C–Cl are 415 and 339 kJ mol^-1, what is the energy released when one mole of CH3Cl is formed from its gaseous atoms (three C–H bonds and one C–Cl bond)?
Complete: (a) A system that can exchange energy but not matter is called a ______ system. (b) Enthalpy is a ______ function.
State true or false: (a) An isolated system exchanges neither energy nor matter. (b) The enthalpy of formation of an element in its standard state is unity.
(a) Write the Gibbs–Helmholtz equation. (b) What is the sign of ΔG for a spontaneous reaction?
Fill in: (a) Heat absorbed at constant pressure equals ______. (b) Heat absorbed at constant volume equals ______.
Match: (a) ΔH > 0 (b) ΔS > 0 (c) ΔG < 0 with (i) spontaneous (ii) endothermic (iii) increased disorder.
Give the signs of ΔH and ΔS for (a) melting of ice (b) combustion of methane.
questions.answer: (a) ΔH positive, ΔS positive. (b) ΔH negative, ΔS roughly positive (small change in disorder, gases formed).

questions.q: State true or false: (a) Work is a state function. (b) ΔG° = −2.303RT log K.
questions.answer: (a) False – work is a path function. (b) True.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What is meant by an isolated system? Give an example.
questions.answer: A system which exchanges neither energy nor matter with its surroundings, e.g. a substance in a perfectly insulated thermos flask.

questions.q: What is the enthalpy of fusion? Write its sign.
questions.answer: The enthalpy change when one mole of a solid melts to form a liquid at its melting point; ΔfusH is positive (endothermic), e.g. ice: +6.0 kJ mol^-1.

questions.q: State Hess's law of constant heat summation.
questions.answer: The total enthalpy change of a chemical reaction is the same whether it takes place in one step or in a number of steps, as enthalpy is a state function.

questions.q: Calculate ΔH for H2 + Cl2 → 2HCl using bond enthalpies: H–H 436, Cl–Cl 243, H–Cl 431 kJ mol^-1.
Differentiate between state function and path function.
questions.answer: State function depends only on the initial and final states (U, H, S, G); a path function depends on the path followed (work and heat).

questions.q: Define standard enthalpy of formation. Give an example.
questions.answer: The enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements in their standard states at 298 K and 1 bar, e.g. C(graphite) + O2(g) → CO2(g), ΔfH° = −393.5 kJ mol^-1.

questions.q: What is entropy? Predict its sign for the evaporation of water.
questions.answer: Entropy is a measure of the randomness or disorder of a system. On evaporation, disorder increases, so ΔS is positive.

questions.q: Calculate the enthalpy change when 2 mol of water is formed (ΔfH° of H2O(l) = −286 kJ mol^-1).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Calculate ΔrH° for N2O4(g) + 3CO(g) → N2O(g) + 3CO2(g), given ΔfH° (kJ mol^-1): N2O4 = +9.16, CO = −110.5, N2O = +81.6, CO2 = −393.5.
State and explain the first law of thermodynamics. Write its mathematical form.
questions.answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be converted from one form to another. The change in the internal energy of a system equals the heat absorbed plus the work done on it: ΔU = q + w. For expansion against external pressure, w = −p_ext ΔV.

questions.q: Derive the relation ΔH = ΔU + Δn_g RT and calculate ΔH − ΔU for N2 + 3H2 → 2NH3 at 300 K (R = 8.314 J K^-1 mol^-1).
Explain the spontaneity of a reaction in terms of ΔH, ΔS and ΔG. Discuss the four possible cases.
questions.answer: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. (1) ΔH −, ΔS +: always spontaneous. (2) ΔH +, ΔS −: never spontaneous. (3) ΔH −, ΔS −: spontaneous at low temperature. (4) ΔH +, ΔS +: spontaneous at high temperature.

questions.q: Calculate the heat evolved when 35.2 g of CO2 is formed by burning carbon, given C(s) + O2(g) → CO2(g), ΔH = −393.5 kJ mol^-1 (C = 12, O = 16).
questions.answer:
Moles of CO2 = 35.2/44 = 0.8 mol.
Heat evolved = 0.8 × 393.5 = 314.8 kJ.

questions.q: Differentiate between an open, closed and isolated system with examples.
questions.answer: Open: exchanges both matter and energy (water in an open beaker). Closed: exchanges only energy (water in a sealed metal vessel). Isolated: exchanges neither (substance in an ideal thermos flask).

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: (a) What is a state function? Name three. (b) State Hess's law and give two applications. (c) The enthalpies of formation of CO2 and CO are −393.5 and −110.5 kJ mol^-1. Find ΔH for C + ½O2 → CO and CO + ½O2 → CO2 from the data.
questions.answer:
(a) A property that depends only on the state of the system: U, H, S, G, T, P.
(b) The total enthalpy change is independent of the route; used to find the enthalpy of formation of compounds that cannot be made directly (CO) and in calculating the lattice energy.
(c) C + ½O2 → CO: ΔH = −110.5 kJ. CO + ½O2 → CO2: ΔH = −393.5 − (−110.5) = −283 kJ.

questions.q: (a) Define the enthalpy of combustion. (b) Explain how the bond enthalpy data are used to calculate ΔH for a reaction. (c) Calculate ΔH for CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O given C–H 414, O=O 498, C=O 804 and O–H 464 kJ mol^-1.
questions.answer:
(a) The enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is completely burnt in oxygen at standard conditions.
(b) ΔH = Σ bond enthalpies of bonds broken in reactants − Σ bond enthalpies of bonds formed in products.
(c) Broken: 4 × 414 + 2 × 498 = 1656 + 996 = 2652. Formed: 2 × 804 + 4 × 464 = 1608 + 1856 = 3464.
ΔH = 2652 − 3464 = −812 kJ.

questions.q: (a) Define Gibbs energy. (b) Write the conditions of spontaneity. (c) For a reaction ΔH = −40 kJ and ΔS = −100 J K^-1 find the temperature below which it is spontaneous.
questions.answer:
(a) G = H − TS, the maximum useful (non-expansion) work obtainable from a process at constant T and p.
(b) ΔG < 0 spontaneous; ΔG = 0 equilibrium; ΔG > 0 non-spontaneous.
(c) ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = 0 at T = ΔH/ΔS = −40000/−100 = 400 K; below 400 K, ΔG is negative, so the reaction is spontaneous.

questions.q: Explain the first law of thermodynamics and calculate q, w and ΔU when 1 mole of an ideal gas expands isothermally into vacuum; then explain what changes if the process is adiabatic.
questions.answer:
ΔU = q + w; for an ideal gas expanding into vacuum p_ext = 0, so w = 0; isothermal means ΔU = 0 for an ideal gas, hence q = 0.
In an adiabatic process q = 0, so ΔU = w: if the gas does work, its internal energy and temperature fall; if work is done on it, its temperature rises.
